subject: Payment Failed
message: Update your payment details immediately or your account will be suspended.
tip: Fake Netflix domain using a lookalike letter
reasons: Lookalike domain: capital 'I' replaces lowercase 'l' in 'Netflix'
Unofficial TLD: '.xyz' is not used by Netflix (real: netflix.com)
Urgent language: 'immediately' pressures you to act without thinking
Threat of suspension: classic scare tactic to steal credentials

subject: Semester Timetable
message: Your semester timetable is now available on the student portal.
tip: Genuine university email no red flags
reasons: Official domain: '.edu.au' is reserved for Australian universities
No urgency or threats: neutral, informational tone
No request for personal data or login credentials
Message matches what you'd expect from a university system

subject: Urgent Login Alert
message: Suspicious activity detected. Verify now to avoid suspension.
tip: Fake PayPal using a hyphenated third-party domain
reasons: Fake domain: PayPal only uses 'paypal.com' never a hyphenated domain
Urgent subject line: 'Urgent' is a common phishing trigger word
Vague threat: 'suspicious activity' with no specific details
Pressures immediate action: 'Verify now to avoid suspension'

subject: New Playlist For You
message: We picked some songs based on your recent listening history.
tip: Genuine Spotify email: standard marketing message
reasons: Official domain: 'spotify.com' with no extra subdomains or hyphens
No urgency or threats: a friendly, low-pressure message
Personalised but benign: references listening history, not credentials
No links to login pages or requests for personal information

subject: Tax Refund Available
message: A tax refund is ready. Claim within 24 hours or it will expire.
tip: Fake ATO using wrong TLD and artificial deadline
reasons: Wrong TLD: Australian Tax Office only uses 'ato.gov.au', never '.net'
Artificial deadline: '24 hours' creates panic to skip verification
Too good to be true: unexpected refunds are a classic phishing lure
Hyphenated domain: 'ato-refund-fast' mimics ATO but is unrelated

subject: New Sign-In Detected
message: A new login was detected on your account from Melbourne, Australia.
reasons: Official domain: 'github.com' with no modifications
Specific detail: includes city/country: phishing emails are usually vague
No action demanded: informs you without pressuring an immediate click
Standard security notification format used by real platforms

subject: Account Verification Required
message: Verify your identity immediately to prevent your account being suspended.
tip: Subdomain trick: the real domain is verify-user.net, not google.com
reasons: Subdomain spoofing: 'accounts.google' is a subdomain of 'verify-user.net'
Real domain rule: the actual domain is always the part before the last '/'
Urgent language: 'immediately' and 'suspended' push you to click fast
Google never asks you to verify via a non-google.com link
